نَجْدَةٌ , a simple subst. (M, L,) Courage, (S, M, L, Msb, K,) and sharpness, or vigour and effectiveness, in those affairs which others lack power or ability to accomplish: (M, L:) or courage with steadiness, and calmness in awaiting fearlessly death, victory, or martyrdom: (EshShiháb [El-Khafájee]:) or great valour: or quickness in assenting to that which one is called or invited to do, whether it be good or evil. (M, L.) ―
-b2- ذُو نَجْدَةٍ A man possessing valour. (S, L.) See مُنَاجِدٌ. ―
-b3- نَجْدَةٌ Fight; combat; battle. (L, K.) ―
-b4- Terror; fright. (L, K.) ―
-b5- Difficulty; distress; affliction; adversity: (Lh, S, * L, Msb, * K: *) pl. نَجَدَاتٌ (Msb.) Ex. لَاقَى فُلَانٌ نَجْدَةً Such a one experienced difficulty, distress, trouble, or adversity. (Lh, S, L.) ―
-b6- See also a saying of Sakhr-el-Ghei, and a citation from a trad., voce رِسْلٌ. ―
-b7- نَجْدَةٌ Aid; assistance. (Msb.) ―
-b8- هُوَ ٱبْنُ نَجْدَتِهَا (tropical:) He is ignorant thereof: contr. of هو ابن بَجْدَتِهَا. By نجدة is meant an allusion to Nejdeh El-Harooree. (A.) See نَجَدٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
